members.reason: ["Blocked on a precise source gap, not on the legal merits. I read the complete official text of EO 7724 (2 FR 2467, signed 1937-10-08, establishing the Bitter Lake Migratory Waterfowl Refuge in Chaves County, New Mexico; the page also carries the end of the previous order, which I did not treat as part of EO 7724) and confirmed identity and a single-clause inventory (the dossier inventory is one clause over the whole body). Its own terms state no end, and its sentence that the reservation supersedes the temporary withdrawal made by Executive Order No. 5909 is a self-executing supersession of that earlier withdrawal, performed in 1937. The gap: the Office of the Federal Register disposition lead says EO 7724 was revoked in part by Public Land Order 326 (1946-08-30, 11 FR 10298). Public Land Order 326 is not in the held corpus (the dossier lists the acting identity as absent from the census, and no text of it is registered in this packet), so I cannot read which lands it removed from the reservation or whether it touched the refuge reservation itself, the proviso that private lands join the refuge on acquisition, or the naming provision. A held later instrument that may have ended a clause cannot be resolved from the held bytes. The three machine searches add no other ending. Missing source: the official text of Public Land Order 326 (11 FR 10298) registered for this order, or a held current-law text showing what remains of the refuge reservation."]

["Blocked on a precise source gap, not on the legal merits. I read the complete OCR text of EO 10789 (23 FR 8897, signed 1958-11-14; Part I paragraphs 1 to 15 and Part II paragraphs 21 to 24, with the preamble and paragraph 4 badly garbled by the three-column scan) and confirmed identity from the heading, the contents entry and the signature date. The dossier inventory (20 clauses) is mis-cut across unrelated Federal Register contents and a Civil Service rule on the same pages and would need an override. I also read the later orders that name it: EO 11051 (1962-09-27, strikes an agency from paragraph 21), EO 11382 (1967-11-28, agency list in paragraph 21), EO 11610 (1971-07-22, adds paragraph 1A on indemnification and amends paragraph 11), EO 11896 (1976) and EO 12143 (1979) which only recite it, EO 12148 (1979, adds an agency to paragraph 21), EO 12919 (1994-06-03, deletes the Proclamation 2914 recital from the preamble), EO 13232 (2001-10-20, adds an agency to paragraph 21) and EO 13286 (2003-02-28, replaces an agency in paragraph 21 and adds Part III paragraph 25 limiting paragraph 1A after March 1, 2003). None ends the order; each is an amendment or recital. On the merits the order would be submitted as operative with these attached. The gap: for EO 11051, EO 11610 and EO 13286 the only registered copies in this packet are American Presidency Project mirror transcriptions and clause-drafts copies; the working-text check rejects them because official Federal Register copies of those three orders are held in the corpus (jobs/fr-originals) but are not registered in this packet's source catalogue, so none can be cited as the source of its later event. EO 11610 (paragraph 1A and paragraph 11) and EO 13286 (Part III paragraph 25, which narrows paragraph 1A) are material amendments that must be attached, and omitting them would leave held later instruments unattached. A second, smaller gap: the garbled preamble and paragraph 4 mean the clause text for those two provisions cannot be quoted or confirmed from the held bytes. Missing sources: a packet whose dossier registers the official texts of EO 11051, EO 11610 and EO 13286 for the EO 10789 pair, and a cleaner text layer of the 1958 original."]

["Blocked on a precise source gap, not on the legal merits. I read the held official text of EO 10173 (15 FR 7005, signed 1950-10-18; the preamble finding, Part 6 of 33 CFR with its definitions, enforcement, access, anchorage, identification and security provisions) and confirmed identity from the heading, title and date. The order is not a short list of commands but the text of regulations that became 33 CFR Part 6, and the later held orders rewrite them section by section: EO 10277 (1951-08-01) amends sections 6.04-1, 6.10-1 and 6.10-7 and adds subparts 6.14 and 6.19, EO 10352 (1952-05-19) and EO 11249 amend further sections, EO 13143 (1999-12-01) rewrites section 6.01-4, EO 13273 (2002-08-21) amends the regulations and EO 14116 (2024-02-21) rewrites sections 6.01-3 and 6.01-5 and adds section 6.01-7. The dossier inventory has only four coarse clauses (the first two spans cover about 12,000 characters and the third about 8,500) and would need a section-by-section override. The gap: whether each section of the original regulations still stands, was replaced, or was redesignated cannot be decided from the held bytes. The continuing text of these regulations lives in 33 CFR Part 6, but no held byte-for-byte copy of the current Part 6 (or of the Coast Guard rules that have since revised it) is registered in this packet; the current-law job outputs are leads only and cannot be quoted. Without it I cannot say, for any section the later orders do not mention, that the original wording is the wording now in force, and several later orders (EO 10352, 11249, 13273) were not resolvable one section at a time from the registered texts, so a held later instrument may have ended or replaced a clause I cannot resolve. Missing sources: the current 33 CFR Part 6 text through 2026-10-14 registered for this order, and the section-by-section dossier inventory for the original regulations."]

["Blocked on a precise source gap, not on the legal merits. I read the held official text of EO 12957 (60 FR 14615, signed 1995-03-15, prohibiting transactions with respect to the development of Iranian petroleum resources and declaring a national emergency under IEEPA and the National Emergencies Act) and the later held orders that name it (EO 12959 of 1995, EO 13059 of 1997, EO 13553 of 2010 and EO 14382 of 2026-02-06, which recites it). Its sections rest on a national emergency that lapses each year unless the President continues it by a notice before the anniversary (50 U.S.C. 1622(d)). The gap: no continuation notice is held. The missing instruments are the yearly Presidential notices continuing the national emergency declared in EO 12957, each published before March 15, for every year from 1996 through 2026 (31 notices), the latest being the one due before March 15, 2026, within the checked-through date of 2026-10-14. The held EO 14382 (2026-02-06) recites that EO 12957 declared the emergency but is not a continuation notice and does not itself say the emergency was continued in 2026. Without those notices the continuing basis of the emergency orders through 2026-10-14 cannot be shown from held bytes. Missing sources: the annual 'Continuation of the National Emergency With Respect to Iran' notices, 1996 to 2026."]

["Blocked on a precise source gap, not on the legal merits. I read the held official text of EO 13553 (75 FR 60567, signed 2010-09-28, blocking property of certain persons with respect to serious human rights abuses by the Government of Iran) and its section structure. It acts 'with respect to the national emergency declared in Executive Order 12957' of March 15, 1995, so its commands last only as long as that emergency is continued each year under the National Emergencies Act. The held later orders that bear on it are EO 12957 (the emergency order) and EO 14382 (2026-02-06), which names it as one of the Iran orders. The gap: no continuation notice is held. The missing instruments are the yearly Presidential notices continuing the Iran national emergency declared in EO 12957, each published before March 15, for every year from 2011 (the first after this order) through 2026, the latest due before March 15, 2026, within the checked-through date of 2026-10-14. Without them the continuing basis for EO 13553's blocking and related sections through 2026-10-14 cannot be shown from held bytes. Missing sources: the annual 'Continuation of the National Emergency With Respect to Iran' notices, 2011 to 2026."]
